movimento: Em pé, com os pés na largura dos ombros e os joelhos soltos, segura a barra por cima (pegada pronada: as palmas viradas para o corpo e o dorso das mãos para a frente), com as mãos na largura dos ombros, e deixa os braços quase esticados, com a barra na frente das coxas. Com os cotovelos parados junto do tronco, o tronco parado e o punho reto (a mão na linha do antebraço), dobra só os cotovelos e sobe a barra até a altura dos ombros, na frente deles — no meio do caminho as palmas ficam viradas para o chão e, em cima, para a frente; só no fim os cotovelos vão um pouco à frente. Desce devagar até quase esticar os braços de novo, sem deixar o punho dobrar.

cinesiologia.plano: sagital, cadeia cinética aberta, os 2 braços juntos
cinesiologia.articulacoes: cotovelos (flexão na subida, de ~16° a ~128°; extensão na descida) com o antebraço pronado o tempo todo e o punho reto (a mão na linha do antebraço); ombros quase parados — o braço fica junto do tronco até o antebraço passar da horizontal e só no fim vai ~8° à frente (leve flexão do ombro); escápulas um pouco pra trás e paradas; tronco, quadril, joelhos (soltos, ~7°) e pés parados
cinesiologia.agonistas: braquiorradial e braquial na flexão do cotovelo. A ExRx põe a rosca inversa no diretório do braquiorradial, com ele de alvo ("Target: Brachioradialis"); com o antebraço pronado o tendão do bíceps enrola no rádio e o braquiorradial trabalha mais (Kleiber 2015: "a significant increased muscular activity of brachioradialis during elbow flexion in pronated compared to supinated and neutral hand position whereas activity of biceps brachii remains constant" — no Boland 2008 a ativação dele não mudou com a posição do antebraço e, no Coratella 2023, foi maior com a supinada: o tamanho do aumento não é consenso). O braquial, preso na ulna, flexiona em qualquer pegada (NSCA: "Brachialis • Flexes elbow joint • Works best with a pronated forearm"; Yessis: "in this exercise, it is the main muscle involved"). No mapa do app o braquial faz parte do grupo "biceps" e o braquiorradial e os extensores do "antebraco": os 2 grupos ficam vermelhos (catálogo: "Braquiorradial · braquial · extensores do antebraço"). Concêntrica na subida e excêntrica na descida
cinesiologia.sinergistas: bíceps braquial (ExRx: "Synergists: Brachialis, Biceps Brachii"), em desvantagem com a pegada pronada (Yessis: "the biceps tendon is wrapped halfway around the radius, which creates a very poor line of pull"; Coratella 2023: a ativação do bíceps na subida foi a menor com a pegada pronada — "the lowest biceps brachii excitation was found with the forearm pronated")
cinesiologia.estabilizadores: extensores do punho, que seguram a mão na linha do antebraço (ExRx: "Wrist Extensors" entre os estabilizadores; Coratella 2023: "the pronated grip is expected to require greater wrist stabilization, especially towards the wrist extension"; Yessis: "this exercise is also effective in developing the forearm muscles especially the wrist extensors"); deltoide anterior, coracobraquial, trapézio (fibras de cima e do meio) e levantador da escápula (ExRx: "Stabilizers: Deltoid, Anterior; Coracobrachialis; Trapezius, Upper; Trapezius, Middle; Levator Scapulae; Wrist Extensors"; o deltoide anterior trabalhou mais com a pronada que com a supinada no Coratella 2023); abdominais e eretores da espinha seguram o tronco parado (Yessis: "Be sure to hold an erect trunk position throughout the execution.")
cinesiologia.fases: subida concêntrica até a barra na altura dos ombros (free-exercise-db: "Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.") e descida excêntrica controlada até quase esticar (ACE: "Slowly lower the weight to return to the starting position."; Yessis: "lower the weights under control back to the starting position")

Yessis M. — Reverse Biceps Curl (Dr. Yessis SportLab, https://doctoryessis.com/2013/01/01/reverse-biceps-curl/, lido em 11/10/2026): "Assume a well-balanced standing position with your feet approximately shoulder-width apart. Hold a barbell with a pronated grip (palms facing down, toward the rear) and with the hands shoulder-width apart."; "Your arms should hang down straight but not locked and your trunk should be erect with the shoulders back."; "Hold the upper arms in place so that the elbows remain alongside the body as you raise the weights."; "After reaching the uppermost position, hold for a count of two and then lower the weights under control back to the starting position."; "Be sure to hold an erect trunk position throughout the execution. Do not drive the hips forward to get the weights moving especially if they are heavy."; "In order to isolate the action to only elbow flexion, be sure that you hold the elbows in place. If you, instead, move the elbows forward you will bring in use of the anterior deltoid and it will decrease the emphasis on the brachialis muscle."; "Because the biceps brachii is a strong supinator of the forearm, it cannot function in this action because of the pronated grip. In this grip, the biceps tendon is wrapped halfway around the radius, which creates a very poor line of pull"; "Be sure to use a barbell as it is more effective for insuring a pronated grip throughout execution."; "The brachialis muscle is a true elbow joint flexor. Since it attaches to the ulna, it is equally effective whether the hand is pronated, supinated, or in a neutral position. This is why, in this exercise, it is the main muscle involved."; "The muscles of the forearm play a very important role in stabilizing the elbow joint as well as the wrist. Thus, this exercise is also effective in developing the forearm muscles especially the wrist extensors. This is why you should maintain the hand in line with the forearm throughout execution. Do not allow the wrist to flex." (o Yessis diz que o braquiorradial "does not play a major role" na pronada — diverge da ExRx, que o põe de alvo)

Kleiber T, Kunz L, Disselhorst-Klug C. Muscular coordination of biceps brachii and brachioradialis in elbow flexion with respect to hand position. Front Physiol. 2015;6:215 (texto completo, PMC4526813, lido em 11/10/2026): "Subjects were measured in standing position with shoulder neither flexed nor abducted."; flexão "from full extension (approx. 0°) to maximal flexion (approx. 130°)"; "As in pronated, the muscular activity of brachioradialis is constantly higher than in supinated and neutral hand position whereas the percentage activity of biceps brachii is nearly the same in all hand positions."; "But in pronated hand position the biceps tendon is wrapped by its insertion in tuberosida radii"; conclusão: "This has been shown by a significant increased muscular activity of brachioradialis during elbow flexion in pronated compared to supinated and neutral hand position whereas activity of biceps brachii remains constant."

Boland MR, Spigelman T, Uhl TL. The function of brachioradialis. J Hand Surg Am. 2008;33(10):1853-9 (resumo, PubMed 19084189, lido em 11/10/2026): "No difference in muscular activation was found during elbow flexion tasks in the 3 forearm positions."; "The greatest EMG activity recorded from the brachioradialis occurs during elbow flexion tasks regardless of forearm position indicating that the primary function of the brachioradialis is as a consistent elbow stabilizer during flexion tasks."

Coratella G, Tornatore G, Longo S, Toninelli N, Padovan R, Esposito F, Cè E. Biceps Brachii and Brachioradialis Excitation in Biceps Curl Exercise: Different Handgrips, Different Synergy. Sports (Basel). 2023;11(3):64 (texto completo, PMC10054060, lido em 11/10/2026): rosca em pé dos 2 braços, na polia com barra de 42,5 cm, com a pegada supinada, a pronada e a neutra — "Each exercise was performed in a standing position. The arms were maintained parallel to the trunk, with no flexion of the humerus."; "The participants were instructed to avoid sagittal oscillations of the trunk, any movement of the lower limbs, and exaggerated elevation of the scapulae"; bíceps: "a greater nRMS was observed with the supinated compared to the pronated [+19(7)%, p < 0.001, ES: 2.60]"; "the lowest biceps brachii excitation was found with the forearm pronated, while the excitation of brachioradialis was similar in the neutral and pronated condition"; braquiorradial: "nRMS was greater with the supinated compared to the pronated [+5(4)%, p = 0.007, ES: 1.01]"; deltoide anterior: "nRMS was greater with the pronated and neutral handgrip compared to the supinated condition"; "the pronated grip is expected to require greater wrist stabilization, especially towards the wrist extension, so as to involve further muscles such as the extensor carpi and other wrist extensors."; "Brachialis is the most powerful flexor of the forearm and, unlike the biceps brachii and brachioradialis, does not insert on the radius, therefore not participating in the forearm supination."

Marcolin G, Panizzolo FA, Petrone N, Moro T, Grigoletto D, Piccolo D, Paoli A. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ. 2018;6:e5165 (texto completo, PMC6047503, lido em 11/10/2026): a pegada pronada NÃO é uma das 3 variações — "Dumbbell curl (DC) and barbell curl in its two variants, straight (BC) or undulated bar (EZ)"; o artigo só cita, de um manual de fisiculturismo, que "performing barbell curls with a reverse handgrip resulted in an increase in brachioradialis activation (Hatfield, 1993)"; "A standing posture was maintained during the performance of the three exercises"; "Trunk movements together with knee flexions were visually monitored by the researchers to avoid possible cheating."; amplitude do cotovelo na rosca com barra reta "BC = 117.3° ± 10.9°"
